result.title: Tracing Attacker Diversity Reduction in Adaptive LLM Red Teaming
result.summary: Reinforcement learning can increase the success of automated red teaming but it also narrows the attack vector. This study asks where in the attacker-defender-judge learning loop does the narrowing begin and which mechanisms lead to a narrowing attack. Six mechanisms (defender adaptation, success edge, reward reinforcement, row cap, update size, and measurement) are tested across three experiment arms (co-trained, frozen defender, half learning rate) for twenty-four iterations. A frozen defender narrows attack diversity retention (ADR) earlier 0.496 relative to co-trained 0.891 at iteration twelve. Defender updates delay narrowing but dont prevent it. Successful attacks ("winners") have narrower attack diversity than the full set of generated attacks. Attacks closest to previous winners succeed 10-15 percentage points more often than those closest to previous failures. This winner-neighbor advantage holds after a defender update and for a fixed defender too. Attacks with a common opening have a common-opening advantage of 5-16 percentage points. The training row cap and update size account for little impact on ADR, and attack length accounts for only part of the ADR decrease. Narrowing appears to originate from the success only reward through the group-relative training advantage to the attacker update, with a persistent success edge setting the direction.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在自适应LLM红队循环中追踪攻击多样性下降的起点，通过六个机制、三条实验臂（联合训练、冻结防御者、半学习率）做二十四轮测试，发现仅以成功为奖励经组相对优势传导至攻击者更新是收窄主因。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「成功奖励—组相对优势—策略更新」导致行为多样性坍缩的分析，可能为核查RL训练下latent推理状态与轨迹的多样性、信息坍缩及信用分配提供类比线索，但领域相距较远，需较多核查。
